rules.statement: In production code, set `HttpClient.Timeout` to `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` on a named or typed client whose calls a resilience pipeline bounds, so the pipeline's options are the only bound.
rules.why: The default 100-second `HttpClient.Timeout` silently cuts a longer configured total timeout.
rules.check: Look for an HttpClient registration with a resilience/timeout handler that leaves `HttpClient.Timeout` at its default or sets it to a finite value.

rules.statement: Retry an outbound HTTP request only when it is safe to send twice: a GET or HEAD with no body; never resend a request that has content or a non-idempotent method such as POST.
rules.why: A retry could replay content an attempt already consumed, and OAuth endpoints honor no idempotency key, so an authorization code or refresh token must never be sent twice.
rules.check: Look for a retry strategy or loop that applies to every request, or to POST/PUT/PATCH or requests with `Content`, without a predicate that limits it to bodiless GET/HEAD.

rules.statement: Never resend a request that carries a `DPoP` proof through a generic retry; only a `use_dpop_nonce` error (RFC 9449 §8) sends it once more, with a new proof carrying the supplied nonce.
rules.why: A DPoP proof's `jti` is single-use (RFC 9449 §11.1), so replaying the same proof is rejected.
rules.check: Look for retry predicates that do not exclude requests with a `DPoP` header, or nonce handling that reuses the old proof or retries more than once.

rules.statement: Order an outbound call's resilience strategies as total timeout outermost, then retry, then per-attempt timeout, and give every outbound call at least the total timeout.
rules.why: The total timeout bounds the whole call including retries and body read, while the per-attempt timeout stops a provider that accepts the connection and never answers from holding the whole budget.
rules.check: Look at pipeline builder calls for a different order, a missing per-attempt timeout on retried calls, or a call path with no total timeout.

rules.statement: Make an HTTP retry handle `HttpRequestException`, the attempt timeout's `TimeoutRejectedException`, and statuses 408, 429 and 5xx, with exponential backoff and jitter, and don't let `Retry-After` extend the delay past the total timeout.
rules.why: These are the transient failures, jitter avoids synchronized retries, and the endpoint must not choose the delay because the total timeout is the bound.
rules.check: Look for retries with constant or unjittered delays, retries on other 4xx statuses, missing handling of attempt timeouts, or code that waits on `Retry-After`.

rules.statement: Dispose every `HttpResponseMessage` a retry discards before sending the next attempt.
rules.why: An undisposed discarded response holds its connection and buffers.
rules.check: Look for retry logic or `OnRetry` callbacks that drop the previous outcome's response without disposing it.

rules.statement: Build retry and timeout behavior from `Polly.Core` strategies, not a hand-written retry loop, and don't add `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` (or `AddStandardResilienceHandler`) to a shipping package.
rules.why: Polly's strategies are tested, and the standard resilience package brings Telemetry plus a circuit breaker and rate limiter the client doesn't need.
rules.check: Look for `for`/`while` retry loops around `SendAsync`, or new references to `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` in shipping projects.

rules.statement: Surface a resilience-pipeline timeout like `HttpClient.Timeout` does, as a `TaskCanceledException` with a `TimeoutException` inner exception, and never report a cancellation by the caller's token as a timeout.
rules.why: Callers distinguish timeouts from their own cancellation the same way they do for HttpClient's built-in timeout.
rules.check: Look for code that lets `TimeoutRejectedException` escape, or that maps any `OperationCanceledException` to a timeout without checking whether the caller's token was cancelled.

rules.statement: Validate outbound-call timeout and retry options when the host starts: timeouts within a bounded range, the attempt timeout no greater than the total timeout, and retry count and delay bounded.
rules.why: An invalid combination must stop the host instead of misbehaving at call time.
rules.check: Look for new timeout/retry options with no startup validator, or a validator that doesn't check AttemptTimeout <= TotalTimeout and the ranges.

rules.statement: Name outbound HTTP resilience options `TotalTimeout`, `AttemptTimeout`, `MaxRetryAttempts` and `RetryDelay`, matching the existing outbound HTTP options, so the family uses one vocabulary.
rules.why: Consistent option names across packages make them one vocabulary for operators.
rules.check: Look for new resilience options with other names such as `Timeout`, `RetryCount` or `Backoff`.

rules.statement: Create a library's `Meter` through `IMeterFactory`, not with `new Meter(...)`, when recording retry and timeout counters.
rules.why: The source requires the meter to come from `IMeterFactory`, which ties its lifetime to the host's DI container.
rules.check: Look for `new Meter(` in library code, or retry/timeout counters on a meter that wasn't created through `IMeterFactory`.
